nodes.summary: A continuous nonnegative compactly supported cutoff normalized on every left orbit meeting `K`, for a closed-embedding homomorphism `ι`. The measure may have any scale. No Hausdorff or countability hypotheses are required.
nodes.title: Continuous cutoff for a closed-embedding homomorphism

nodes.summary: A continuous nonnegative compactly supported Bruhat cutoff for a closed subgroup, normalized on any subset of the saturation of a compact set.
nodes.title: Continuous Bruhat cutoff for a closed subgroup

nodes.summary: A Bruhat section: given a closed subgroup `T` of a locally compact group and a set `E` contained in `T * C` for compact `C`, there is a compactly supported nonnegative measurable function `w` whose integral over each `T`-translate meeting `E` equals `1`.
nodes.title: Existence of a Bruhat section for a closed subgroup

nodes.summary: A compact set in a topological group with a compact open subgroup has a nonnegative locally constant cutoff whose integral over every left `T`-orbit meeting that set is one, for a closed commutative subgroup `T`. The same compactly supported function works simultaneously on all of `T * Ω`. The Haar measure need not have any prescribed normalization.
nodes.title: Existence of a locally constant normalized subgroup cutoff

nodes.summary: A compact cocompactness witness gives a continuous normalized cutoff and a positive common integral for all nonnegative measurable compactly supported normalized cutoffs. Every such cutoff is genuinely integrable, even when it is not bounded. Neither the ambient group nor the subgroup must be Hausdorff.
nodes.title: Positive common integral of cocompact subgroup cutoffs

nodes.summary: Integrability of an invariant complex function times a nonnegative real weight is independent of the weight when both orbit averages are one on the function's support. Neither weighted function is required to be integrable.
nodes.title: Integrability is independent of the orbit-normalized weight

nodes.summary: A bounded measurable `T`-invariant complex function is integrable against any nonnegative measurable compactly supported weight whose `T`-average is one wherever the function is nonzero. The weight need not be bounded.
nodes.title: Bounded invariant functions are integrable against normalized cutoffs

nodes.summary: The integral of a bounded measurable `T`-invariant complex function against a nonnegative measurable compactly supported cutoff does not depend on the cutoff, when each cutoff has subgroup integral one on the support of that function. Normalization is not required outside its support.
nodes.title: Cutoff independence of integrals of bounded invariant functions

nodes.summary: Weighted integrals of an invariant complex function agree for nonnegative orbit-normalized cutoffs. If one weighted function is not integrable, neither is the other, and both Bochner integrals are zero.
nodes.title: Orbit-normalized cutoffs give equal complex integrals

nodes.summary: Subgroup-normalized nonnegative weights give the same integral of an invariant complex function. This measure-theoretic statement requires neither a closed subgroup nor compact supports nor a bounded function.
nodes.title: Subgroup-normalized weights give equal integrals

nodes.summary: Nonnegative integrals of an invariant function agree for orbit-normalized weights. Normalization is needed only where the function is nonzero, and the common integral is allowed to be infinite.
nodes.title: Orbit-normalized weights give equal nonnegative integrals

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
